title: Write evidence-based dashboard insights
description: Write observations, plausible explanations, missing evidence and recommended checks separately.
accomplishes: Write observations, plausible explanations, missing evidence and recommended checks separately. Refer to actual values only when provided. Prioritise decisions over decorative commentary and do not turn correlations into causes or incomplete data into confident conclusions.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Write evidence-based dashboard insights.

Input context:
- REPORT: [REPORT]
- METRIC DEFINITIONS: [METRIC DEFINITIONS]
- PERIOD: [PERIOD]
- DECISION: [DECISION]

Write observations, plausible explanations, missing evidence and recommended checks separately. Refer to actual values only when provided. Prioritise decisions over decorative commentary and do not turn correlations into causes or incomplete data into confident conclusions.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Insight-writing example
Observation: the supplied report has more enquiries but no qualification history. Possible explanation: reach or tracking changed; neither is established. Next check: compare deduplicated events and CRM outcomes for equivalent periods. Avoid calling the change profitable until costs and completed sales are known. This example deliberately leaves unsupported conclusions unresolved.
